findings.title: Design aligns with slice plan entry 25 and architecture scope
findings.description: The slice design covers all three parts the slice plan assigns (Part A: record truncation, Part B: cap truncated+unread PASS, Part C: record answering model) and stays within the maintenance initiative's scope — no new features, just recording facts about existing runs and closing a correctness gap. Exclusions match the plan's "not in scope" list (defaults, #114). Diff ordering and `--stat` are deferred to #137, which the plan explicitly permitted ("in scope only if design shows it is small; otherwise it becomes an issue"). The design's three parts are independently deliverable per the architecture's guidelines.

findings.title: VerdictSource.IMPOSED addition is justified and bounded
findings.description: The existing `VerdictSource` enum (verified in `src/squadron/review/models.py:28-30`) is a closed two-value vocabulary (`STATED`, `DERIVED`) whose docstring says it was kept closed to avoid open reason strings. The design's D5 adds `IMPOSED` and argues the docstring's concern was about reason strings, not member count — which is accurate reading of the existing docstring. The design verifies no external reader consumes `verdictSource` (grep of context-forge) and that only `impose_diff_coverage` sets it. This is a contract expansion that is well-justified and properly bounded.

findings.title: aiModel semantic change is the highest-risk integration point
findings.description: The design changes `aiModel` from the requested model to the answering model. This is a semantic change to an existing consumed contract (context-forge gates, metrology identity). The design's argument — "That is the meaning its consumers assumed all along" — is reasonable but is an assertion about external consumer assumptions, not a verified claim. The metrology consequence (D10: OpenAI-direct judges change identity once, from `gpt-5` to `gpt-5-2025-08-07`) is acknowledged and accepted as correct calibration. This is not a blocking issue since the design explicitly calls out the consequence and the change is in the direction of correctness, but it is the integration point most likely to surprise a downstream consumer and warrants the design's stated care.

findings.title: Failure modes for all provider-reporting paths are enumerated
findings.description: The design enumerates handling for every provider-reporting case: normal match (D10), dated snapshot (D9/D10), substitution (D9/D10), provider reports nothing/Codex (D11), multiple models in one run (D12), and provider-failure artifacts with no answer (D13). Each has an explicit strategy, not "TBD." The "not reported" case (D11) is deliberately not a silent fallback — the artifact states it in the Run Digest. No new I/O paths are introduced; the design instruments existing git-diff and provider-stream paths, so no new hang/timeout/disconnect enumeration is required.

findings.title: Proportionality — mechanism count fits the slice
findings.description: The design introduces three focused mechanisms (DiffInjection accounting, impose_diff_coverage rule, answering-model stamping) across a reasonable set of components. The `answers_as_requested` regex rule (D9) is the heaviest piece, but the design explicitly avoids speculative model-id forms and defers real-id capture to Phase 6 verification (walkthrough step 6), which is the lighter approach. The design names what can be cut: file-body truncation (#138), diff ordering (#137), and judge-findings `round_diff` are all excluded with issue references. No abstraction is introduced that nothing uses — `DiffInjection` is consumed by Part A rendering, Part B's cap, and the JSON contract.

findings.title: Interface parity between CLI and pipeline paths is structural
findings.description: Both `sq review` and the pipeline `review` action call `run_review_with_profile` then `save_review_result` → `format_review_markdown`, and every new fact rides `ReviewResult`. The design explicitly states "No second code path to keep in sync" and success criteria SC1 and SC12 verify both paths. This matches the interface-parity requirement the slice plan implies and that prior slices (916, 919) enforced.
